The error in (4) is checked. When outside air is hotter, its density falls, so less air mass flows through the gas turbine compressor and output drops. A combined cycle is therefore affected more by outside temperature than a steam power plant. The explanation's cause-and-effect is correct.

(1) Start/stop is fast. (2) Load following is good. (3) Thermal efficiency is higher because the Brayton and Rankine cycles are combined.
